title: Delete the Middle Node of a Linked List
description:
You are given the `head` of a non-empty singly linked list of length `n`. Delete the **middle node** located at 0-based index `floor(n / 2)` and return the `head` of the modified list.

If the list has only 1 node, deleting it produces an empty list (`null` / `None`).
constraints: The number of nodes in the list is in the range [1, 10^4].
hints: Handle the single-node base case (`head.next == null`) by returning `null` directly.
Give `fast` a two-step head start (`fast = head.next.next`) while `slow = head` so that when `fast` reaches the end, `slow` points to the node immediately **before** the middle node.

examples.explanation: For length 7, floor(7 / 2) = 3 (node with value 7) is removed, leaving [1, 3, 4, 1, 2, 6].
For length 4, floor(4 / 2) = 2 (node with value 3) is removed, leaving [1, 2, 4].
For length 1, deleting the only node leaves null.
